text:
maria: Proposal — experiment with a stochastic wait/coalesce policy for continuous batching. Instead of fixed coalesce_delay we sample waiting time from a distribution so short requests can go immediately while slightly delaying medium requests to improve packing. thinking Poisson/exponential sampling with a tunable base and clamp.

aj: curious — what problem are we targeting? tail latency or cost? both trade off. also worried about KV cache priming if we delay too often.
maria: both. primary goals: reduce p99 token-cost while keeping p99 latency below 350ms for 2k token requests. Secondary: avoid thrashing KV cache warmups for hot keys. Idea: use base_delay_ms + sampled_jitter where sample ~ Exp(lambda). clamp to [0, max_delay]. adjust lambda by queue depth and per-model token budget.
rahul: quick profiling from last week to set baselines:
```
Baseline (current fixed 5ms coalesce): p50=22ms, p95=88ms, p99=240ms, throughput=450 tokens/s per GPU, avg batch size=3.1 requests
With 10ms fixed: p50=28ms, p95=110ms, p99=290ms, throughput=520 tokens/s, avg batch size=4.4
KV hit-rate during slotting windows: 87% (spikes drop to 73% on heavy jitter)
```
This suggests small increases in average delay improve throughput but blow up tail. Stochastic might preserve quick paths for single-shot and still boost packing.
kyle: can we make lambda adaptive? e.g., lambda = f(queue_length, recent_latency_tail). If queue is empty, sample -> 0 almost always. If high queue + low tail, increase mean wait. avoids unnecessary delays.
maria: yes — my config sketch:
```
batching:
  strategy: stochastic_coalesce
  base_delay_ms: 2
  max_delay_ms: 20
  sampler: exponential
  lambda_map:
    low: 1.5   # mean ~0.67ms
    medium: 0.3 # mean ~3.3ms
    high: 0.08  # mean ~12.5ms
  adapt_window_s: 5
  kv_protection: true  # avoid delaying requests that hit same kv key within x ms
  token_budget_target: 1200
```
Note: lambdas tuned to yield sub-ms to 10+ms tails. kv_protection prevents delaying requests that would prime a cache entry needed by imminent reqs.
aj: how do we detect "same kv key within x ms" cheaply without adding overhead? naive memcmp on key slices might be expensive.
rahul: cheap heuristic: keep an LRU bloom/sketch of recent key hashes at 1s resolution. if key present, bypass coalesce (or reduce sampled delay). sketch false positives are fine (we'll skip delay unnecessarily sometimes rather than introduce cache miss). memory tiny.
kyle: need to instrument two metrics for A/B: 1) per-request KV-hit-after-coalesce (did delaying create a miss later), 2) batch entropy (how diverse tokens/keys inside a batch). add histograms for sample values and batch sizes.
maria: agreed. Also add an experiment arm with 'poisson jitter' vs 'exponential sampling' to compare long tail behaviour. Poisson inter-arrival sampling might be more natural for arrival smoothing when clients are bursty.
rahul: perf regression risk: kernel selector currently picks kernels based on observed batch-size distribution. If distribution shifts (more varied batch sizes) selector could pick suboptimal kernels mid-rollout. Need a guard: pin kernels for rollout window or add hysteresis to kernel selection.
aj: good catch. we should snapshot kernel choice metrics pre-rollout and compare. if kernel mismatch rate > 7% rollback.
maria: rollout plan I propose:
1) Canary on 10% of traffic for least-sensitive models (low token budgets) with kv_protection off. collect 1h data.
2) If no p99 > baseline+40ms and no >2% regression in KV-hit-rate, expand to 50% with kv_protection on.
3) Full rollout with kernel-pinning hysteresis and auto-rollback on kernel_mismatch >7% or tail bursts.
kyle: add unit tests for sampler determinism and a reproducible runner for the fuzz harness.
maria: small snippet for telemetry we'll add to request logs: `stochastic_wait_ms`, `sampler_lambda_level`, `kv_sketch_hit`. plan to feed to console dashboard charting.
rahul: on the profiling side, also capture per-token compute ms vs queue wait ms so we can attribute p99 spike to compute vs queuing. current traces often conflate both.
maria: nice. I'll draft a PR with config + e2e smoke tests. can someone volunteer to own the canary dashboard?
aj: I can. will add batch entropy and kv-hit heatmaps to the dashboard.
kyle: I can do the sampler unit tests and skew-fuzz harness.
maria: thanks. I'll open the RFC and attach the perf numbers and rollout checklist.
